conversation.content:
Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to experience a wide range of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being in the postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during this time. By using the EPDS, we can get a better sense of how you're feeling and identify any areas where you might need some extra support.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. I want you to feel comfortable and at ease throughout our conversation.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us explore your emotional experience over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible.

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually enjoy, or have you been feeling a bit down or disconnected from activities that normally bring you pleasure?

.. to be honest, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but it's just been really hard to enjoy the things I used to like doing. Even simple things like taking a shower or reading a book feel like chores now. I just don't have the energy or the motivation like I used to. And when I do try to do something I normally enjoy, it just doesn't feel the same. It's like the joy is just... muted, you know? 

I've been feeling really sad and discouraged a lot of the time, and I just can't seem to shake it off. I worry all the time about my baby's safety, and sometimes those thoughts just spiral out of control. I'll be sitting there, feeding her or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and it's hard to calm myself down. It's like my mind is just racing all the time.

I do try to push through, though, because I don't want to be a bad mom. I feel guilty when I'm not enjoying the time with my baby, like I'm somehow failing her. But at the same time, I just feel so... drained. Like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really living. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll catch myself smiling when my baby does something cute, but it's not like I'm really laughing like I used to. It's more like... a polite smile, you know? I'm just going through the motions. I don't really feel like I'm enjoying things or finding the humor in life like I used to. Even when my husband tries to make me laugh, it's just not the same. I'll smile, but inside, I'm still feeling really down and overwhelmed. 

Sometimes, when I'm feeling really anxious or worried about the baby, I'll try to distract myself by watching a funny video or something, but even that doesn't really work. I'll be watching it, and I'll be thinking, "Oh, this is funny," but I'm not really feeling it. It's like my brain is just numb or something. And then I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do, or all the things that could go wrong, and it just spirals out of control. (pausing, looking down) Sorry, it's just... it's hard to explain. I just don't feel like myself anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Not really. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like... a chore. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or meeting a friend for coffee, just feel like too much effort now. I'll think about doing something, and then I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the things I need to do to make it happen, like packing up the baby's stuff and finding someone to watch her... it just feels like too much.

And even when I do manage to do something I used to enjoy, it's just not the same. Like, my husband and I went out for dinner last week, and I was really looking forward to it, but then I just ended up worrying the whole time about the baby and whether she was okay with the babysitter. I couldn't even enjoy my dinner because I was just sitting there, thinking about all the things that could be going wrong at home. (sighing) It's just hard to feel like I can really look forward to things and enjoy them when I'm always worried about something else.

Sometimes, I'll think about doing something nice for myself, like taking a relaxing bath or reading a book, but then I'll just feel guilty about it. Like, I'll think, "I should be using this time to do something more productive, like laundry or cleaning," instead of taking time for myself. It's like I'm always putting myself last, and that just makes me feel more down and overwhelmed.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Oh, yeah... that's definitely something I've been doing a lot of lately. I mean, if the baby cries, I immediately think it's because I'm not doing something right, or that I'm not a good enough mom. If she's not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine, or that I'm not doing enough to help her sleep. It's like, no matter what happens, I always seem to find a way to blame myself for it.

And it's not just with the baby, either. If I'm feeling overwhelmed or tired, I'll think, "Well, if you were just more organized, or if you just managed your time better, you wouldn't be feeling this way." It's like I'm always criticizing myself, and it's just really hard to shake off that feeling of guilt and self-doubt.

Sometimes, my husband will try to reassure me, and he'll say things like, "You're doing a great job, you're an amazing mom," but it's hard for me to really hear that and believe it. I just feel like I'm always falling short, and that I'm not living up to my own expectations of what a good mom should be. (looking down, getting a bit choked up) It's just really hard to be kind to myself, I guess.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, that's me all the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, I'll think, "What if she chokes on something?" or "What if I'm not producing enough milk?" or "What if I'm not doing enough to stimulate her development?" It's just constant, and it's exhausting.

And the worst part is, it's not even like I can rationalize it away. I'll be like, "Okay, self, you're being ridiculous, there's no reason to worry about this," but the worry is just still there, gnawing at me. It's like my brain is just constantly looking for things to worry about, and it's hard to turn it off.

Sometimes, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, I'll think about the baby's health, or our financial situation, or our relationship as a family... it's just this never-ending list of things to worry about. And I'll be lying there, feeling my heart racing and my mind racing, and I'll just feel so... anxious. Like, I'll be physically anxious, you know? My stomach will be doing flips, and my hands will be shaking... it's just really hard to calm down.

(sighing) And it's not even like I can talk to my husband about it, because he just gets frustrated with me. He's like, "You're being paranoid, everything is fine," but he doesn't get it. He doesn't understand what it's like to be constantly worried and anxious all the time. (shaking my head) It's just really hard to explain, but it's just this constant feeling of dread, like something is always lurking just beneath the surface, waiting to go wrong.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath) Yeah, that's happened to me a few times. I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like, my body is reacting like I'm in danger or something, but there's no reason for it. It's just... (shaking my head) it's really scary, actually.

Sometimes, it'll happen when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, I'll think about the baby getting hurt, or me not being able to take care of her, and it'll just spiral out of control. I'll start to feel like I'm not in control, like I'm just losing my grip on everything. And that's when the panic sets in.

It's hard to describe, but it's like my body is just... reacting, you know? It's like my fight-or-flight response is just triggered, and I don't know how to calm it down. I'll try to breathe deeply, or remind myself that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic.

And the worst part is, it's not just the panic itself, it's the fear of losing control. Like, I'll think, "What if I'm not a good mom? What if I'm not capable of taking care of this baby?" And that just makes the panic worse, because I feel like I'm not just scared, I'm also... (pausing, looking for the right words) I'm also inadequate, I guess. Like, I'm not good enough to be a mom.

(looking down, getting a bit choked up) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard to talk about this stuff. But I guess it's good that I'm talking about it, right? (nervously laughing)
Things have been getting on top of me

(sighing) Yeah, that's an understatement. I feel like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it's just all so overwhelming. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make dinner, and the baby will be crying, and the phone will be ringing, and I'll just feel like I'm losing my mind.

I feel like I'm constantly running on empty, you know? I'm exhausted all the time, but I don't have the luxury of just taking a break. I have to keep going, no matter how I'm feeling. And it's hard, because I feel like I'm not doing anything well. I'm not being a good mom, I'm not being a good partner, I'm not being a good friend... I just feel like I'm failing at everything.

And the worst part is, I feel like I'm all alone in this. My husband tries to help, but he doesn't really get it. He doesn't understand what it's like to be a new mom, to be responsible for this tiny human who depends on you for everything. And my friends... they're all busy with their own lives, and they don't really get it either. They'll say things like, "Oh, just sleep when the baby sleeps," or "Just ask for help when you need it," but it's not that easy. It's not that simple.

(looking up, tears in my eyes) Sometimes I just feel like I'm drowning, you know? Like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, but everything is just pulling me under. And I don't know how to make it stop. I don't know how to make myself feel better, or how to make my life feel more manageable. I just feel like I'm stuck, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding) Yes, that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. I mean, that's part of it, but it's also because my mind is just racing all the time. I'll be lying in bed, trying to fall asleep, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that are bothering me. I'll think about the baby, and whether I'm doing a good job as a mom, and whether I'm providing enough for her. I'll think about my relationship with my husband, and whether we're doing okay. I'll think about all the things I need to do, and all the things I'm not doing.

And it's not just that I'm thinking about these things, it's that I'm feeling really overwhelmed by them. I'll feel anxious, and worried, and just... unhappy, I guess. And that makes it hard to fall asleep, because my mind is just going a million miles an hour. I'll be lying there, feeling like I'm wide awake, and I just can't seem to calm down.

Sometimes, I'll manage to fall asleep, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll be wide awake again. And it's not just because the baby needs to be fed, or changed, or something. It's because my mind is just racing, and I'm feeling really unsettled. I'll lie there, thinking about all the things that are bothering me, and I'll just feel so... trapped, I guess. Like I'm stuck in this cycle of unhappiness, and I don't know how to get out of it.

(sighing) It's hard, because I know that sleep is important, especially when you're a new mom. But it's just... my mind is not cooperating, I guess. And it's not just the sleep itself, it's the feeling of being unrested, and unrefreshed. I'll wake up in the morning, and I'll feel like I've been hit by a truck. I'll feel exhausted, and grumpy, and just... unhappy. And that's not a good way to start the day, especially when you're trying to take care of a new baby.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Yes, that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just walking around in a cloud of sadness, all the time. It's not just that I'm feeling a little down, or a little blue. It's like I'm really struggling to find any joy, or any happiness, in my life right now.

As a mom, I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, and grateful, and all those things. But the truth is, I'm just feeling really overwhelmed, and anxious, and sad. I feel like I'm not doing a good job, as a mom, or as a person. I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, most of the time.

And it's not just the big things that are getting to me. It's the little things, too. Like, I'll be trying to get the baby to sleep, and she'll just refuse to settle down. Or I'll be trying to make dinner, and I'll just feel so exhausted, and overwhelmed. And it's like, I just feel like I'm at my breaking point, all the time.

I feel like I'm crying all the time, too. Like, I'll just be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying. It's not even like I'm thinking about anything, in particular. It's just like, my emotions are just so raw, and so close to the surface, all the time.

(sighing) I guess what I'm trying to say is, I just feel really sad, and really miserable, a lot of the time. And I don't know how to make it stop. I don't know how to make myself feel better, or how to find any joy, in my life right now. I just feel like I'm stuck, in this rut of sadness, and I don't know how to get out of it.

(looking down, tears streaming down my face) Sorry, I'm just... I'm really struggling, right now. I feel like I'm just barely holding on, most of the time. And I don't know how much longer I can keep going, like this.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Yes, that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me, and I'll start crying. It's not even like I'm thinking about anything, in particular. It's just like, my emotions are just so raw, and so close to the surface, all the time.

I've been crying in front of my husband, in front of my friends, even in front of the baby. It's like, I just can't help it. I feel like I'm just so overwhelmed, and so sad, and I don't know how to make it stop. I've tried to hold it in, to just push through and be strong, but it's just not working. The tears just keep coming, and I feel like I'm just losing control.

It's not just the big things that make me cry, either. It's the little things, too. Like, I'll be trying to get the baby to sleep, and she'll just refuse to settle down, and I'll just start crying. Or I'll be trying to make dinner, and I'll just feel so exhausted, and overwhelmed, and I'll start crying. It's like, I'm just so sensitive, and so emotional, all the time.

(sighing) I feel like I'm just crying all the time, and it's getting to the point where I'm just feeling so embarrassed, and so ashamed. I feel like I'm just not a good mom, or a good person, because I'm just so emotional, and so weak. But at the same time, I feel like I'm just not allowed to feel this way. Like, I'm supposed to be happy, and grateful, and all those things, but I'm just not.

(looking down, tears streaming down my face) I guess what I'm trying to say is, I just feel really overwhelmed, and really sad, and I don't know how to make it stop. I feel like I'm just crying all the time, and I don't know how to make myself feel better. I just feel like I'm stuck, in this rut of sadness, and I don't know how to get out of it.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pause, looking down, struggling to speak) Yeah... I've had those thoughts. (pausing again, taking a deep breath) It's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I've ever thought about before. But since having the baby, I've just felt so overwhelmed, and so trapped, and so... hopeless, I guess. And sometimes, when things just seem too much, I've had those thoughts. (looking up, tears in my eyes) It's like, I just feel like I'm not doing a good job, and I'm not a good mom, and I'm just... I'm just not worthy of love, or care, or anything.

(voice barely above a whisper) It's not like I've ever seriously considered it, or made any plans, or anything. It's just... it's just a thought that's occurred to me, when things have been really tough. And it's scary, because I don't know where it's coming from, or how to make it stop. (pausing again, taking a deep breath) I guess what I'm trying to say is, I'm just really struggling, and I don't know how to make it better. And sometimes, when things seem too much, I just feel like... I don't know, like I'm just not sure if I can keep going, I guess.

(looking down, tears streaming down my face) I'm so sorry to say that. I feel like I'm just... I'm just a terrible person, for even thinking that way. But I guess I just needed to be honest, and say it out loud. (pausing, looking up) I just want to feel better, and I don't know how to make that happen.
